metadata.title: LMC origin of the hyper-velocity star HE 0437-5439. Beyond the supermassive black hole paradigm

evidence.quote: LMC origin of the hyper-velocity star HE 0437<sub>−</sub>5439

Stars moving faster than the Galactic escape velocity were first
predicted to exist by Hills (1988). The first such hyper-velocity
stars (HVSs) were discovered serendipitously only recently
(Brown et al. 2005; Hirsch et al. 2005; Edelmann et al. 2005,
E05: HE 0437−5439 at 723 km s<sup>−1</sup> heliocentric radial velocity).

Edelmann et al. (2005) found the early B-type star HE 0437−5439 to
be too short-lived to have reached its current position in the Galactic halo if ejected from the GC, except if being a blue straggler star.

values.condition: Derived in this paper from the revised non-LTE analysis, with Z ≈ 0.013 and evolutionary tracks.

evidence.quote: The corresponding distance to HE 0437−5439 is 61±9 kpc, in perfect agreement with E05.

values.condition: Distance inferred by Edelmann et al. (2005) from a main-sequence interpretation based on an LTE analysis.

evidence.quote: This put the star at a distance of ≈60 kpc.

values.condition: Heliocentric radial velocity reported by Edelmann et al. (2005).

evidence.quote: E05: HE 0437−5439 at 723 km s−1 heliocentric radial velocity

notes: HE 0437−5439: The conclusion refers to “HE 0437−3954” at T:p4-b3, T:p4-b4, T:p4-b5 and T:p4-b7. This is treated as a typographical error for HE 0437−5439—the HVS identified at T:p1-b1 and T:p1-b11 and analysed in T:p2-b5—so the erroneous designation is not recorded as a separate identifier.

HE 0437−5439: The conclusion occasionally refers to “HE 0437−3954”, evidently a transcription/printing error for HE 0437−5439; this does not affect the extracted results. No right ascension, declination, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame total speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for the target.
